subject: Dedicated GPU pool: provisioning window & burst policy alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@auroraai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisioning window + capacity forecast (Aurora AI)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Were ready to move forward with a dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads and I wanted to get the provisioning logistics on your calendar so we can align on burst/autoscale behavior. Attached is our initial capacity forecast for the first 90 days.

Quick context:
- Peak concurrent QPS per model: ~220 (two models: ranking + generation)
- Typical sustained QPS: ~70
- P95 response SLA target: <250ms
- Primary region preference: us-west-2 (we have a small presence in eu-west-1)

Questions we have up-front:
1) Typical lead time youd need to provision a new GPU pool in us-west-2 and what the maintenance window looks like.
2) What burst mechanism do you recommend for spiky traffic (pre-warmed nodes vs short-lived burst allocation)?
3) Can you confirm what telemetry and runbooks you provide during the cutover?

Attached: aurora_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Would appreciate a short call this week to lock dates.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of ML Infrastructure | Aurora AI
j.ellis@auroraai.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@auroraai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisioning window + capacity forecast (Aurora AI)

Jordan,

Appreciate the forecast and clear ask. Looping in Marissa (on implementation) and Tessa (CS lead) so we can coordinate the activation. Answers inline below and proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- Lead time: 9-12 business days for a fully staged pool in us-west-2 if we push the provisioning request this week.
- Burst mechanism: hybrid approach. Well configure a pre-warmed standby set (warm nodes for <5s response) plus short-lived burst allocation (ephemeral GPUs) with a cap tied to burst credits. This gives predictable cold-start behavior and controlled unit cost.
- Telemetry/runbooks: we provide a pre-cutover checklist, a live cutover dashboard (token-level latency + queue depth), and a triage runbook for fallback to a smaller hosted model variant.

Proposed provisioning window: 2028-08-07 01:00 UTC -> 2028-08-09 18:00 UTC (includes smoke tests and rollback buffer). Please confirm if that works for Aurora.

Information we need from you to lock the plan:
- Confirm final expected peak concurrency (220 is fine, we just need to validate per-model distribution).
- Desired burst cap (suggested starting cap: +35% of peak = ~300 concurrent across models).
- Any regulatory requirements around region failover or data residency.

Next steps:
1) You confirm the window or propose alternatives.
2) We send the activation MLP + SOC2 evidence package (attached for your review).
3) We schedule a 60-minute cutover dry-run on 2028-08-03.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@auroraai.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jul 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisioning window + capacity forecast (Aurora AI)

Jordan / Alex,

Following up with the implementation details from the activation team. Ive attached a trimmed SOC2 evidence bundle and our standard activation checklist. Highlights and recommended defaults below:

- Initial pool size: we recommend provisioning for sustained load + 25% buffer. For your numbers that maps to ~100 sustained GPUs with a 25% buffer for baseline.
- Burst policy: default config we use for first-activation customers is: pre-warmed set of 8 nodes, burst credit limit = 2x baseline for short spikes (max 4 minutes per burst), and a cooldown period of 15 minutes between bursts.
- Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at queue depth > 12 and scale-down when CPU/GPU utilization < 22% for 5 continuous minutes.
- Fallback routing: automatic fallback to a quantized model variant (q4) if P95 latency exceeds 400ms for >2 minutes.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-evidence.zip (application/zip), activation_checklist_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

If Aurora wants a more aggressive burst cap we can increase the credit limit, but that will impact cost and wed recommend a 2-week post-activation observation before raising caps.

Marissa Cole
Head of Implementation | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks team - thats helpful. A few clarifying items from Aurora ops: 

- The 220 concurrent is split roughly 60/40 between ranking and generation respectively. Well validate this in the spreadsheet but that aligns with our telemetry.
- Regional fallback: we need the ability to fail over to eu-west-1 in the event of sustained us-west-2 disruption. Can you outline the failover time SLA and any limitations (e.g., stateful KV caches not being replicated)?
- Monitoring: wed like a link to the cutover dashboard and a contact list for on-call during the 48-hour activation window.

Also, confirm that the pre-warmed nodes will be reserved (billed as reserved capacity) vs billed as ephemeral.

On scheduling: the proposed window looks fine. Please send calendar invites for the dry-run and the activation.

—Sam
